title: Hanoi traffic police trace a missing 78-year-old on the city's new AI camera network; a passer-by finds him hypoglycaemic in Dịch Vọng at 3 a.m.
summary: Hanoi police traced a lost 78-year-old on AI traffic cameras on 15 Dec 2025; a passer-by found him at 3 a.m. the next day and took him home.
account: Mr Đ.V.T., 78, of Thanh Xuân ward, Hanoi, went out to exercise at 3:30 p.m. on 15 December 2025 and did not return; at 8:15 p.m. his family reported him to Thanh Xuân Ward Police. Ward officers worked with the Hanoi Traffic Police Department, where Major Nguyễn Tá Khanh's team searched the AI traffic-camera system in the direction the family gave and traced him along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and other streets; VietNamNet and Tiền Phong say the images were posted on social media. At about 3 a.m. on 16 December a passing resident found him in Dịch Vọng, hypoglycaemic and close to fainting, and took him home. No source links the finder to the appeal.
purpose: Hanoi's AI traffic-camera system (1,837 cameras with AI-controlled signals, due to enter official operation in December 2025, per VOV) is run by the Traffic Police, in VOV's words, 'to ensure security and order and support the people' as well as to manage traffic; tracing a lost resident for a ward police search falls within that stated remit.
system: Hanoi Traffic Police AI traffic-camera system (1,837 cameras)
deployer: Hanoi City Police, Traffic Police Department (Phòng Cảnh sát giao thông), with Thanh Xuân Ward Police
segment: Missing elderly person traced on urban traffic cameras
taxonomy_note: Locating a missing person is not among the six types; Organizational Efficiency is chosen, as for the other search records, because the documented gain is search direction and speed for the police, while the benefit itself is the man's safe return.

ratings.reason: A 78-year-old who had been out for nearly twelve hours on a December night was home by about 3 a.m., found hypoglycaemic and close to fainting; he and his family got him back safely, though the finder was a passer-by rather than the police.

Thanh Xuân Ward Police and the Traffic Police got a direction of travel and images from the camera trace instead of a blind search, and the police present the case as evidence of the new system's value.

ai_role.statement: The system's contribution was the trace: searched in the direction the family gave, it returned images of the man walking along Nguyễn Tuân street toward Thanh Xuân Park and across other streets, which gave the police a route and pictures for a public appeal. He was found by a passing resident in Dịch Vọng about eleven hours after the report; no source says the finder had seen the appeal or that officers reached him, so the discovery itself is not attributable to the system. The vendor is not named and every account comes from the police.

produced_by: A dense AI camera network along the route the person walked, here 1,837 cameras across Hanoi, with footage searchable by appearance and direction of travel.
A family report the same evening giving a starting point and a direction for the camera search.
A ward police unit able to hand the search to the Traffic Police's camera-control team the same night.
must_hold: The missing person stays within camera coverage; here the trace ended at a route, not at the man, and a passer-by made the find.
Someone acts on the trace or the appeal; the sources do not establish that link in this case.
The vendor and the matching method are undisclosed, so the trace cannot be checked beyond the police account.

headline: Hanoi traffic police trace a lost 78-year-old on AI cameras

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and six Vietnamese reports of 17 December 2025. Kept at benefit created or restored as the classifier proposed: the camera trace is documented, but the man was found by a passing resident and no source links the finder to the trace or the appeal, so no prevented harm is evidenced. The rank Thiếu tá is rendered as Major. VOV reports that the 1,837-camera system was to begin official operation in December 2025, so this was among its first publicised cases. The Phụ Nữ Online link redirected to a tuoitre.vn mirror path when fetched on 20 October 2026; the original URL is cited. The 8:15 p.m. report time and the 3 a.m. find are consistent across VnExpress, VietNamNet, Tuổi Trẻ, Tiền Phong, VOV and Phụ Nữ Online.
